subject: Linguistics
title: Bilingualism
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bilingualism usable.

hook.text: More than half the world's population speaks two or more languages. Monolingualism is the exception.

buildup.text: Bilingualism can be simultaneous (from birth) or sequential (second language learned later).

discovery.text: Bilinguals don't have two separate brains—both languages are active and interact constantly.

twist.text: Bilingual children may mix languages—but this isn't confusion; it shows sophisticated grammar knowledge.

climax.text: Research shows bilingualism enhances executive function—the brain's ability to control attention.

punchline.text: Two languages, one brain—and it's sharper for it.

quiz.question: How does bilingualism affect the brain?
